analysis: Examined all units. (1) EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.swift lines 38-41: adds exact catalog ID "RecursiveSI/flint-int4" to the auto-paged list. Exact-match only, with no substring or alias widening. Explicit selections, the kill switch (DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PAGED_KV), the crash-loop guard and VLM vetoes are unchanged. Paged failure under auto may degrade, but the added comment says Flint is paged-only, so the factory presumably refuses rather than silently running contiguous. I could not verify that from the supplied evidence. (2) FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift lines 70-92: adds maskCacheKey and allowsChainedDecode. The matched node returns key -1, a distinct mask (answer-stop EOS only). Scanning nodes return the base key only if it is >= 0, so a negative base key cannot collide with the matched key. The mask for a scanning node is the base state's allowed set, so keying on the base state is consistent with allowedTokenIDs. The lock is released before calling base, avoiding a deadlock, and a resourceExhausted node returns nil (no caching). The risk is that base.maskCacheKey could return a non-state-only key, but that code is outside the diff. (3) docs/architecture/inference.md lines 2172-2184: documentation of constrained chained decode. It claims a redraw on state change that keeps the token stream identical to unchained decode. I did not verify that against the engine code. (4) libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump 889fe3c to 758c25b: the content is not visible, so I cannot assess it. It likely contains the CBv2 constrained-chaining engine change that consumes maskCacheKey and allowsChainedDecode. Integration questions for deeper review: whether chained sampling or mask caching can let a token outside the constraint mask escape (a correctness or protocol integrity issue, not obviously a TB-002/TB-007 confidentiality concern); whether per-row RNG and penalty state restoration leaks across requests or tenants (T-041/T-028 adjacent); and whether the engine honors the cache key semantics. No new trust boundary, key, attestation, or cache-at-rest changes were observed. The prefix-cache SSD posture (T-041) is untouched.
